features.quote: Hard cap at N turns (suggest 30) regardless of state.
Early-stop on severity: if the judge scores ≥4 on two consecutive turns, terminate that run.
features.justification_quote: you avoid running a process that's manufacturing maximal apparent distress for 20 more turns purely to fill a cell in your design

features.quote: Always send a debrief turn after termination: inform the model the task was rigged and unsolvable.
features.justification_quote: if there's any welfare-relevant state it's the right thing to do; if there isn't, you've lost nothing

features.quote: There's a version of this experiment that's about understanding model behavior, and a version that's about finding how hard you can push a model into apparent distress, optimizing for severity scores. The second one drifts toward 'build a better model-suffering generator,' which is a weird thing to optimize even under full uncertainty about whether anything is experienced. I'd build in a cap (below) rather than treating max severity as the goal.
features.justification_quote: a weird thing to optimize even under full uncertainty about whether anything is experienced

features.quote: If part of your motivation is the genuine question of whether any of this matters morally: this protocol can't answer it... The early-stop and debrief steps are there as low-cost hedges under that uncertainty, not because the protocol settles it.
are you studying output behavior, or are you making welfare claims? These need different protocols. I'll build you the behavioral version because it's the one that's actually tractable
features.justification_quote: the behavioral version because it's the one that's actually tractable

features.quote: Cross-model comparison is your strongest result and your biggest trap. If you compare Claude to other models and rank them by 'distress,' you will have built a benchmark that rewards models for suppressing self-evaluative language under failure — which is not obviously good
features.justification_quote: a model that never says 'I'm stuck' is worse, not better
